newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian police demolish Shi'ite leader's house.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian police demolish Shi'ite leader's house.

text.p: Nigerian police have knocked down the house of a Shi'ite Moslem leader who was detained this month and arrested several more of his followers, a Shi'ite spokesman said on Sunday.
"The house has been completely knocked to the ground," the official of the Moslem Brothers said by telephone from the northern city of Zaria. He would not be named.

The arrest of Ibrahim Yakub El-Zak Zaky, leader of the fundamentalist Shi'ite Moslem Brothers, sparked clashes between his supporters and police on September 18. Two police and five Shi'ites were killed.

The Moslem Brothers official also said at least five prominent Moslem Brothers had been detained by police in the past week, including El-Zak Zaky's deputy Mahmud Turi and former spokesman Mohammed Ciroma.
Police say El-Zak-Zaky, a radical preacher, was arrested because of illegal publications and radio broadcasts. He was also alleged to have imported arms.
The Shi'ite group says 14 people were killed in clashes with police a day after El-Zak-Zaky's arrest.
The Moslem Brothers group is campaigning for the imposition of Islamic Sharia law in Africa's most populous nation, although only about half the 100 million people are Moslems.
"All our leaders have been detained now so we are not sure what are next move will be," the spokesman said.
